title: Core: Improve story generation and args extraction
body:
Closes # ## What I did This PR refactors the story generation logic (not save story, but create story) so that it is more detached, does not depend on Storybook to be running and also requires data from docgen and not argtypes directly. Something along the lines of: It introduces a new preset which receives a component file path and export name, and then processes that over docgen (each renderer has to implement their own) and returns argtypes from that. Additionally, there's a new function to generate dummy data based on argtypes, which is much improved and provides more features in the story generation. It now also accounts for handlers and uses `fn` from `storybook/test` and adds the necessary import for that. Here's an example of before/after the new capabilities ## Checklist for Contributors ### Testing #### The changes in this PR are covered in the following automated tests: - [ ] stories - [x] unit tests - [ ] integration tests - [ ] end-to-end tests #### Manual testing 1. Run Storybook 2. Find a good component candidate to try this out, make sure it has types and required args. Also make sure that even for those required types, there are no default values in the prop usage in the component render function. 3. Click on the + button to create a new story for that file 4. Watch the resulting file and see whether it looks correct ### Documentation - [ ] Add or update documentation reflecting your changes - [ ] If you are deprecating/removing a feature, make sure to update [MIGRATION.MD](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/next/MIGRATION.md) ## Checklist for Maintainers - [ ] When this PR is ready for testing, make sure to add `ci:normal`, `ci:merged` or `ci:daily` GH label to it to run a specific set of sandboxes. The particular set of sandboxes can be found in `code/lib/cli-storybook/src/sandbox-templates.ts` - [ ] Make sure this PR contains **one** of the labels below:
Available labels - `bug`: Internal changes that fixes incorrect behavior. - `maintenance`: User-facing maintenance tasks. - `dependencies`: Upgrading (sometimes downgrading) dependencies. - `build`: Internal-facing build tooling & test updates. Will not show up in release changelog. - `cleanup`: Minor cleanup style change. Will not show up in release changelog. - `documentation`: Documentation **only** changes. Will not show up in release changelog. - `feature request`: Introducing a new feature. - `BREAKING CHANGE`: Changes that break compatibility in some way with current major version. - `other`: Changes that don't fit in the above categories.
### 🦋 Canary release This PR does not have a canary release associated. You can request a canary release of this pull request by mentioning the `@storybookjs/core` team here. _core team members can create a canary release [here](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/actions/workflows/publish.yml) or locally with `gh workflow run --repo storybookjs/storybook publish.yml --field pr=`_ ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Automatic dummy prop generation for stories and propagation of args into generated templates (including CSF factory support and customizable preview imports). * Function-placeholder handling so non-primitive props are injected with appropriate helpers. * **Improvements** * Safer story-file creation with clearer result-driven outcomes and overwrite protection. * Improved React component type extraction and richer arg-type mapping. * Extended prop type support (date, node, literal, tuple, etc.). * **Tests** * Expanded test coverage for generation, templates, and docgen extraction. ✏️ Tip: You can customize this high-level summary in your review settings.

The `storyFilePath` returned from `getNewStoryFile()` is constructed using `getProjectRoot()` (see get-new-story-file.ts line 136), but line 77 uses `process.cwd()` for relative path calculation. If the Node.js process is launched from a different directory than the project root, this produces incorrect relative paths.

<summary>🔧 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
 import { relative } from 'node:path';

```

Then, use it for the relative path calculation:

```diff
-    const relativeStoryFilePath = relative(process.cwd(), storyFilePath);
+    const relativeStoryFilePath = relative(getProjectRoot(), storyFilePath);
```
</details>

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
Normally preset preset properties adhere to a system where they can be chained.

So the pattern to adhere to is:
```ts
function<A>(input: A, o: Options): A
```

This `experimental_getArgTypesData`'s input and output are not the same; making it unchainable.

If this is likely to be replaced with some actual system later, that is likely okay for now..

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I can see this is pre-existing code, so hard to do anything about it, but it's generally recommended to avoid using synchronous `fs`-APIs if it can be prevented.

Like I mentioned in our call, I was very much expecting the argType functions to be async, because:

1. It needs to interact with the `fs`
2. We'll want to write these (at some point) for all renderers, and the API will have to be the same for all (since core-server will consume it) Though I guess there's no harm in `await`ing a synchronous value?
